assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with Borel measurable structure and canonical full-space volume, including dimension zero. W is C1, exp(-W) is integrable, and mu is exactly volume.tilted(-W).

D is the original closable partial gradient on L2(mu), with graph exactly compact smooth scalar representatives and their genuine gradients modulo mu-a.e. D is fixed before epsilon>0 and forcing f in L2(mu). The genuine solution u/G/r and all local volume facts are derived, not supplied.

For every C2 real cutoff chi with compact topological support, the same u chosen before all chi yields explicit v=chi*u, Gchi=chi*G+u*grad chi and Fchi=chi*r+2 inner(grad chi,G)+u Delta chi. Neither sign, normalized mass, compact derivative bounds nor localized PDE/H2 certificate is assumed. All localized L2 and test integrals use volume; variational identities use L2(mu).
units.statement: For the exact normalized Gibbs mu, original closable D fixed before epsilon/forcing, construct the actual resolvent u in D.closure.domain. Retain the actual all-domain variational equation, ordinary locally integrable u/G, all C1 compact directional weak-gradient tests, squared local integrability of r=epsilon*u+inner(grad W,G)-f, compact-volume L2 of u/G/r and every C2 original distribution test. For every C2 compact chi define v=chi*u, Gchi=chi*G+u*grad chi, Fchi=chi*r+2 inner(grad chi,G)+u Delta chi. Prove genuine global-volume L2 of v/Gchi/Fchi and each topological support contained in tsupport chi. For every C1 compact psi/direction a both weak-gradient products are L1 with integral psi inner(Gchi,a)=-integral v Dpsi[a]. For every C2 compact phi both PDE products are L1 with integral v Delta phi=integral Fchi phi. The same u is chosen before all cutoffs; only smooth test/cutoff functions have classical derivatives.

steps.title: Choose the same real solution before every cutoff
steps.text: Use the canonical ordinary resolvent producer for the exact Gibbs law and original D. Retain its all-domain variational identity, ordinary gradient/PDE and actual compact-volume L2 of u/G/r. Choose this u once, before quantifying over chi; no cutoff-specific replacement solution or supplied final localized equation is introduced.
steps.formula: \exists u\in\operatorname{dom}\overline D\ \forall\chi\in C_c^2,\quad G=\overline Du,\quad r=\varepsilon u+\langle\nabla W,G\rangle-f.

steps.title: Derive derivative support and global L2
steps.text: The actual Frechet derivative support is contained in tsupport chi; its second derivative and finite-basis Laplacian vanish outside that set too. C2 makes grad chi and Delta chi continuous. Bound their norms only on K=tsupport chi. Actual restricted a.e. measurability and MemLp domination yield the localized scalar/vector/drift L2 on K, then the proven indicator equality and memLp_indicator_iff_restrict give global-volume L2. All three topological supports lie in K. This step does not infer global L1 from global L2.

steps.title: Prove the first weak product rule with legal terms
steps.text: Test the original ordinary weak gradient at chi*psi. Actual Frechet multiplication gives D(chi psi)=chi Dpsi+psi Dchi. Each separate product is L1, using the parent compact-test integrability and the continuous compact multiplier in L infinity. Riesz identifies Dchi[a]=inner(grad chi,a). After legal integral addition, cancel the u psi Dchi term to obtain the localized gradient identity.

steps.title: Compute the actual second test product and cross identity
steps.text: Differentiate the first product again; true C2 second derivatives and finite orthonormal-basis trace give Delta(chi phi)=chi Delta phi+2 inner(grad chi,grad phi)+phi Delta chi. For each b_i test the original weak gradient at phi Dchi[b_i], genuinely C1 compact. Every summand and individual split is L1 using local integrability and continuous compact coefficients before finite sum/integral exchange. Empty sums retain dimension zero.
steps.lean: directional_second; second_product; laplacian_trace; laplacian_product; cutoff_cross_identity; integral_finsetSum

steps.title: Derive the localized PDE with the exact coefficient2
steps.text: Use the original PDE at chi*phi and the preceding product formula. Prove L1 of chi*u*Delta phi, chi*r*phi, the cross term and u*phi*Delta chi individually. Borel normalization merely identifies the given Borel measurable structure with the canonical one; function algebra is normalized without changing the measure. Legal integral splitting and the cross identity yield the positive coefficient2 and positive u Delta chi term in Fchi, with both final tested products integrable.

steps.title: Retain only the proven compact-localization boundary
steps.text: Return the same parent witnesses and all original identities, together with every cutoff result. The ordinary gradient of v is not asserted to equal D.closure applied to v: no membership of v in that weighted closure-domain is proved here. The compact-to-Schwartz/tempered adapter, local H2, global weighted core/Bochner and functional inequalities still need their own producers.
steps.formula: \text{compact localization/global }L^2\quad\ne\quad H^2,\text{ weighted core or BL}.
